caption: The suit was R1 100 and nobody will remember it. What's the most you've spent on a day that wasn't about you?

slides.title:
What unveiling
my father's tombstone
costs on R27 000 p/m
Living in Bhisho
slides.body:
Male, 36
Married, one daughter (4)
Job: Accountant, provincial treasury
Net salary: R27 000 p/m (this month, the unveiling)

slides.title: Tombstone
slides.includes: Granite headstone and installation, second of three instalments
slides.body: My father said nothing about it while he was alive. The family expects it done properly.

slides.title: Catering
slides.includes: Food for about 120 guests, a sheep, cooks
slides.body: My uncles decide the numbers. I decide the bank balance.

slides.title: Tent and sound
slides.includes: Tent, chairs, sound system, generator hire
slides.body: Rented for one Saturday. It rains in Bhisho at the worst times.

slides.title: Groceries
slides.includes: Our usual shop, not the unveiling food
slides.body: My wife keeps the two budgets apart on a sheet of paper. It helps a little.

slides.title: Everything else
slides.includes: Petrol, electricity, aftercare, funeral policy, stokvel, black tax, a new suit
slides.body: I bought a suit for R1 100. I own three. The funeral policy is R420 and the stokvel is R500.

slides.title: What's left
slides.body: Out of R27 000. A tombstone isn't a want. It still has to come out of the same salary.

slides.title: I stopped guessing
slides.body:
I uploaded my statement to Beyond Horizon and it showed what this one month looked like.

The suit was the line I'd already forgotten.

No bank login needed.
